name: get_account_overview
label: Looking at your account
description: Who the signed-in user is and counts across their whole account: channels, groups, private chats, bots, archived chats, chats with unread messages, unread DMs and mentions. Free and instant (local data).

name: list_chats
label: Listing chats
description: Lists the user's chats from local data (free, instant), newest activity first. Use to find chats by name, list channels/groups/DMs, or find chats with unread messages. Each chat includes its id, type, unread counts and a preview of its last message.

name: get_chat_info
label: Getting chat details
description: Details about one chat: description/bio, member count, username, link, unread state.

name: read_messages
label: Reading messages
description: Reads messages from one chat or channel, newest first. Returns post refs to cite. Use since_hours for "today"/"this week", unread_only for what the user hasn't read. Does not mark anything as read.

name: get_recent_activity
label: Catching up on recent posts
description: What's new: reads the latest messages across the chats with activity in the time window, most recent chats first. Best for "what's new today", "what did my channels post". Costs Telegram requests, so keep max_chats modest.

name: search_messages
label: Searching messages
description: Full-text search of messages, in one chat (chat_id) or across all chats. Returns post refs to cite.

name: get_message
label: Opening a message
description: One message in full, with its link. Use when a preview was cut short.

name: show_channel_post
label: Showing a channel post
description: Delivers one channel post into the current AI conversation for viewing, playing, or opening. This never forwards or sends it to Saved Messages.

name: list_contacts
label: Listing contacts
description: The user's Telegram contacts with usernames and last-seen status. Optional name filter.

name: list_chat_folders
label: Listing folders
description: The user's chat folders (e.g. Work, Personal) with how many chats and unread chats each has. Pass folder_id to list the chats in one folder.

name: get_unread_mentions
label: Finding mentions
description: Messages where the user was @mentioned or replied to and hasn't read yet, across all chats.

name: get_pinned_messages
label: Reading pinned messages
description: The pinned messages of a chat or channel, newest first.

name: get_comments
label: Reading comments
description: The comments under a channel post (with who wrote each and their reactions), or the replies in a group thread. Comments live in the channel's discussion group: each has its own ref, usable with react_to_message, get_message_reactions or comment_on_post(reply_to_message_id).

name: list_shared_media
label: Browsing shared media
description: Photos, videos, files, links, voice notes or audio shared in a chat, newest first.

name: search_public_chats
label: Searching Telegram
description: Finds public channels, groups and bots on Telegram by name or @username, including ones the user hasn't joined. Doesn't join anything.

name: send_message
label: Sending a message
description: Sends a message to a chat, or posts in a channel the user can post in, optionally with photos, videos or files. The user sees an editable draft and must approve it before anything is sent; they may change the text or attachments, or decline. Only call when the user asked you to send something. Text may use Telegram formatting: **bold**, *italic*, <u>underline</u>, ~~strikethrough~~, ||spoiler||, `code`, ```code block```, [text](https://link). The other person sees "typing…" or "sending a photo…" first.

name: forward_message
label: Forwarding
description: Forwards one or more messages (several at once, in order) to another chat, or to several chats at once with to_chat_ids, Saved Messages included. Optionally without the sender's name (hide_sender) and without captions (remove_caption). The user must approve it first. Only call when the user asked for it.

name: get_forum_topics
label: Listing topics
description: The topics of a forum group (a group with topics), with unread counts and latest activity. Read a topic with read_messages(chat_id, topic_id).

name: get_user_profile
label: Opening a profile
description: A person's profile: name, @username, bio, last seen, whether they are a contact, their personal channel and the groups you have in common.

name: send_chat_action
label: Showing chat activity
description: Shows a temporary Telegram activity indicator in a chat, such as typing, recording a voice note, uploading media, or choosing a sticker. Use only when the user explicitly asks to show that activity. The user must approve it first.

name: get_chat_presence
label: Checking active status
description: Checks whether a person in a private chat is online, or when Telegram says they were last active. Telegram may deliberately return an approximate status for privacy.

name: send_live_location
label: Sharing live location
description: Gets the phone's current location and shares it in a chat, optionally live for 1 to 1440 minutes. The user must approve it first.

name: browse_stickers
label: Browsing stickers
description: Browses installed, recent and matching Telegram stickers. Results include sticker file ids for send_sticker or save_sticker.

name: browse_gifs
label: Browsing GIFs
description: Browses GIF-style animations shared in one chat. Open a returned post to view it with playback controls, or forward it to send it elsewhere.

name: search_stickers
label: Searching public stickers
description: Searches public Telegram sticker sets by one or more emoji. Use browse_stickers for installed sticker keyword search.

name: send_sticker
label: Sending a sticker
description: Sends a sticker returned by browse_stickers or search_stickers. The user must approve it first.

name: save_sticker
label: Saving a sticker
description: Saves a sticker to the user's Telegram recent stickers. The user must approve it first.

name: web_search
label: Searching the web
description: Searches the web with the user's Exa key and returns source titles, URLs and highlights. Use only when the user asks for web research or current information.

name: react_to_message
label: Reacting
description: Adds an emoji reaction to a message (or removes the user's reaction). The user must approve it first. Only call when the user asked you to react.

name: set_chat_notifications
label: Changing notifications
description: Mutes or unmutes a chat, group or channel (muted: true/false). Use list_chats(include_muted) to see what is muted. The user must approve it first.

name: mark_as_read
label: Marking as read
description: Marks everything in a chat as read (clears its unread badge). The user must approve it first. Only call when the user asked for it.

name: explore_forum
label: Exploring a forum
description: Reads a forum group topic by topic: its topics (pinned and most active first) with the latest messages in each. Use for "what's happening in <forum>".

name: get_message_reactions
label: Reading reactions
description: The reactions on a message: counts per emoji, and who reacted with what where Telegram shows it (groups, and channels the user runs). Works for comments too (use the comment's ref chat id).

name: comment_on_post
label: Commenting
description: Posts a comment under a channel post (or replies to a comment with reply_to_message_id from get_comments). The user sees an editable draft and must approve it. Only call when the user asked you to comment.

name: reply_to_message
label: Replying
description: Replies to a specific message or post, optionally quoting the exact part you answer (quote must be copied word for word from it). By default the reply goes in the same chat; pass send_in_chat_id to reply from another chat, e.g. quote a channel post inside a DM. Files can be attached. The user sees an editable draft and must approve it. Only call when asked.

name: pin_message
label: Pinning
description: Pins a message at the top of a chat, or unpins it (unpin: true). Silent by default; notify: true alerts the members. In a DM, only_for_me pins it just for the user. See current pins with get_pinned_messages. The user must approve it first.

name: edit_message
label: Editing a message
description: Changes one of the user's own messages or channel posts: its text or caption, and/or its media (replace the photo, video, file or audio with one from files, or add one; send_as file keeps it uncompressed). Telegram may refuse to add media to a message that was sent as plain text; the tool says so. The user must approve it first. Only call when asked.

name: schedule_message
label: Scheduling a message
description: Schedules a message (with optional files) to be sent later by Telegram itself, even if this app is closed. The user sees an editable draft and must approve it. Give send_at as local time, or in_minutes.

name: list_scheduled_messages
label: Checking scheduled messages
description: Messages the user has scheduled to send later, with when they go out. One chat, or (without chat_id) the chats with recent activity the user can write in.

name: reschedule_message
label: Rescheduling
description: Moves a scheduled message to another time, or sends it right away. The user must approve it first.

name: archive_chat
label: Archiving
description: Moves a chat into the Archive, or back out to the main list (archived: false). Nothing is deleted. The user must approve it first.

name: remember
label: Remembering
description: Saves something to long-term memory so it is known in every future conversation: preferences, facts about people or chats, standing requests. Use when the user says "remember…", or shares something clearly worth keeping. Keep each memory short and self-contained.

name: update_memory
label: Updating a memory
description: Rewrites a saved memory (ids are listed in your instructions and by list_memories).

name: forget_memory
label: Forgetting
description: Deletes a saved memory, when the user asks you to forget something or it is no longer true.

name: list_memories
label: Checking memory
description: Everything saved in long-term memory, optionally filtered.

name: create_watch
label: Setting up a watch
description: Creates a watch that runs on its own. Triggers: new messages in specific chats (chat_ids), all_dms, all_groups, all_channels, mentions of the user, a folder (these need Telegram), a schedule (daily_at "HH:MM" or every_minutes), or app: something new in a connected app (app = a toolkit like gmail, slack, github, notion, todoist, or "any"; query = what to look for, e.g. "emails from my bank"), checked every_minutes (default 15), or phone: something on the phone (phone_event: battery low, plugged in/unplugged, Wi-Fi joins/leaves, arriving at or leaving a place, a missed call, a new SMS, the user opening the app). tools limits what its runs may use; model picks a cheaper model (free by default). Modes: notify (a phone notification with the new messages), summarize (you write a short note and the user is notified), act (you follow the instructions on every trigger, e.g. reply to each new DM, and may use any tool). Use for "tell me when X posts", "watch my DMs and answer them", "every morning summarise my channels".

name: list_watches
label: Listing watches
description: The user's watches and routines, with what triggers them and what they do.

name: update_watch
label: Changing a watch
description: Changes a watch: turn it on or off, rename it, change its chats, mode, schedule or instructions.

name: delete_watch
label: Removing a watch
description: Removes a watch or routine for good.

name: create_widget
label: Making a home-screen widget
description: Makes a home-screen widget (Android): a scrolling list of rows with optional pictures and links. Give shows to have the assistant keep it up to date every every_hours (subscriber counts, latest news, new movies with posters, weather, a to-do list from an app); a scheduled watch then refreshes it with update_widget. Give items for rows now (for static text, or a first fill). The user adds it from their home screen and picks what each widget shows in Settings → Home-screen widgets.

name: update_widget
label: Updating a widget
description: Replaces a home-screen widget's rows (and optionally its title, what it shows or how often it refreshes). Use it when refreshing a widget or when the user asks to change one.

name: list_widgets
label: Listing widgets
description: Lists the home-screen widgets: the built-in brief and custom ones, what each shows and when it was updated.

name: delete_widget
label: Deleting a widget
description: Deletes a custom home-screen widget and stops its refresh. The brief widget can't be deleted.

name: online_alert
label: Setting an online alert
description: Notifies the user when someone comes online ("tell me when Liya is online"). once: false keeps alerting each time (at most every 15 minutes). remove: true cancels it. Works only if that person lets the user see their last seen (contacts, or everybody); the app keeps running in the background while alerts are set.

name: list_online_alerts
label: Listing online alerts
description: The people the user asked to be told about when they come online, and whether each is online now.

name: notify_me
label: Notifying
description: Shows the user a phone notification now. Useful in watches when something needs their attention; tapping it opens this conversation.

name: generate_image
label: Creating an image
description: Creates an image from a detailed prompt with the image model chosen in Settings. The image is shown to the user in the chat. Use when asked to draw, design or visualize something.

name: get_model_settings
label: Checking the AI models
description: The AI models chosen in Settings (AI & models) for chat, decisions (Jev), images, video and audio, with each model's name, provider and whether it is enabled and ready to use. Audio includes the voice and dictation engines, their models and the selected voice. Reads settings only; no AI call is made.

name: generate_video
label: Creating a video
description: Creates a short video from a detailed prompt with the video model chosen in Settings, optionally starting from a picture in this chat. It is shown to the user in the chat. Videos cost far more than images and take a while: make one only when asked for a video or animation.

name: generate_audio
label: Creating audio
description: Creates an MP3 spoken by the voice selected in Settings. When Addis AI is selected, use an available Addis voice ID (am-, om-, or ti-) to create Amharic, Afaan Oromo, or Tigrinya speech. The audio is shown in the chat and can be sent to Telegram like a generated image.

name: generate_addis_voice
label: Creating an Addis AI voice
description: Creates an MP3 with Addis Voices 2. Use for Amharic (am), Afaan Oromo (om), or Tigrinya (ti). Choose a voice ID from the live Addis AI catalog when the user names one; otherwise an available default voice for the requested language is selected. Requires the user to add an Addis AI key in Settings.

name: generate_sound_effect
label: Creating a sound effect
description: Creates a sound effect or ambience from a description using ElevenLabs. Requires an ElevenLabs API key in Settings → AI & models. The audio appears in chat and is saved in Files. Use generate_music for songs and scores, and generate_audio for speech.

name: generate_music
label: Creating music
description: Creates music, a song or a score from a description using ElevenLabs. Describe the genre, mood, instruments and any vocals. Requires an ElevenLabs API key in Settings → AI & models and access to music generation. The audio appears in chat and is saved in Files.

name: send_voice_message
label: Sending a voice message
description: Sends one recorded voice note to a chat as a Telegram voice message. Use only for a voice-note attachment the user provided in this conversation, and only when they asked to send it.

name: list_attachments
label: Checking files
description: Every file in this conversation that can be sent to a chat: pictures, videos, voice notes and documents the user attached, and images or audio you generated. Pass a name in files to send it.

name: create_poll
label: Creating a poll
description: Posts a poll or a quiz in a chat or channel: 2 to 10 options, anonymous or public, single or multiple answers, or a quiz with one correct answer and an explanation. Can close itself after open_minutes. The user must approve it first.

name: get_poll_results
label: Reading poll results
description: The results of a poll or quiz: votes and percentages per option, whether it is closed, what the user chose, and for public polls who voted for each option.

name: vote_poll
label: Voting
description: Votes in a poll (option indexes from 0), or takes the vote back with an empty list. Needs approval.

name: stop_poll
label: Closing a poll
description: Closes one of the user's polls so nobody can vote any more. Needs approval.

name: send_contact
label: Sharing a contact
description: Shares one of the user's Telegram contacts (or the user themself) as a contact card in a chat. Needs approval.

name: view_image
label: Looking at images
description: Lets you inspect images from any available source: attachments (by name, including earlier messages), generated images, screenshots, downloaded images, local file paths or file URLs, direct HTTP/HTTPS image URLs and image data URLs. For Telegram photos, video thumbnails, GIF frames, stickers and link previews, pass refs "post:<chat_id>:<message_id>". Telegram is only needed for refs. Up to 6 images at once. The selected chat model must support image input. The images come right after the result.

name: download_message_file
label: Downloading a file
description: Downloads the file a Telegram message carries (document, PDF, voice note, audio, video, video note, GIF, photo or sticker) to the phone. Text files come back as text, pictures are shown to you, and the file can then be sent on with send_message or worked on with run_code / e2b_upload_file. For what a voice or audio message says, use transcribe_message.

name: transcribe_message
label: Listening to a message
description: What a voice note, audio file, video note or video says: downloads it and writes out its speech. Uses Addis AI for Amharic and Afaan Oromo, ElevenLabs Scribe, or the dictation model from AI & models, whichever is set up.

name: view_stickers_and_gifs
label: Looking at stickers and GIFs
description: Shows you stickers (file_id from get_sticker_set, list_favorite_stickers or search_stickers) and GIFs (gif_id from search_gifs or list_saved_gifs) as pictures, so you can pick a fitting one before send_sticker or send_gif. Animated ones show their first frame. For a sticker or GIF in a message, use view_image with its ref. Up to 8 at once; the chat model must see images.

name: search_gifs
label: Searching GIFs
description: Finds GIFs on Telegram (through its @gif search) for a word or mood, e.g. "thank you", "facepalm". Returns gif_id values for send_gif.

name: list_saved_gifs
label: Opening saved GIFs
description: The user's saved GIFs, with gif_id values for send_gif.

name: send_gif
label: Sending a GIF
description: Sends a GIF (a gif_id from search_gifs or list_saved_gifs) to a chat. Needs approval.

name: save_gif
label: Saving a GIF
description: Adds a GIF from a message (chat_id and message_id) to the user's saved GIFs.

name: list_sticker_sets
label: Opening sticker packs
description: The sticker packs the user has installed, with set_id values for get_sticker_set.

name: get_sticker_set
label: Opening a sticker pack
description: The stickers in one pack (set_id from list_sticker_sets), with file_id values for send_sticker.

name: list_favorite_stickers
label: Opening favourite stickers
description: The user's favourite and recently used stickers, with file_id values for send_sticker.

name: favorite_sticker
label: Favouriting a sticker
description: Adds a sticker (file_id) to favourites, or removes it with remove: true.

name: list_backgrounds
label: Opening backgrounds
description: Telegram backgrounds installed on the account (wallpapers, patterns, gradients), with background_id values for set_chat_background.

name: get_chat_background
label: Checking the background
description: The background a chat currently uses, if it has its own.

name: set_chat_background
label: Changing the background
description: Sets a chat's background. Give exactly one of: background_id (from list_backgrounds), file (an image the user attached, by name or path), or color / colors (hex like "#1E2A3A"; two colours make a gradient). remove: true restores the default. only_for_me (default true) keeps it on this account; false also sets it for the other person in a private chat. Needs approval.

name: get_bot_buttons
label: Reading bot buttons
description: The buttons on a bot message (chat_id, message_id), row by row, with their kind (callback, url, switch_inline, web_app, reply…). Use before press_bot_button.

name: press_bot_button
label: Pressing a bot button
description: Presses a button on a bot message, by its text or by row/column (0-based) from get_bot_buttons. Callback buttons return the bot's answer; url buttons return the link (not opened); reply-keyboard buttons send their text to the bot. Needs approval.

name: list_calls
label: Opening call history
description: The user's call history, newest first: who, incoming or outgoing, voice or video, how long, and whether it was missed, declined or ended. only_missed: true for missed calls.

name: recently_joined_chats
label: Finding new channels and groups
description: Channels and groups the user joined most recently, with when they joined. days limits how far back (default 30).

name: contact_joins
label: Finding contacts who joined
description: Contacts who recently joined Telegram ("X joined Telegram"), from the user's private chats.

name: export_channel_summary
label: Exporting channel statistics
description: Creates a shareable PNG summary for a channel the user can read: profile photo, name, public link, subscriber count when Telegram exposes it, and average views, shares and reactions from recent posts. Works with public channels too; it does not require admin statistics. The PNG appears in Files and can be sent with send_message by passing its name in files.

name: translate_message
label: Translating
description: Telegram's own translation of a message (chat_id, message_id) into to_language (a code like "en", "es"). Works on Premium accounts or chats with translation on; otherwise translate it yourself.

name: mark_as_unread
label: Marking as unread
description: Marks a chat as unread (or clears the mark with unread: false), like Telegram's "Mark as unread".

name: pin_chat
label: Pinning a chat
description: Pins a chat to the top of the chat list (or unpins with pinned: false). Needs approval.

name: add_chat_to_folder
label: Changing a folder
description: Adds a chat to one of the user's Telegram folders (folder_id from list_chat_folders), or takes it out with remove: true. Needs approval.

name: list_my_chats
label: Listing your channels and groups
description: Channels, groups and bots by the user's role: role "owner" (created by the user), "admin" (owner or admin) or "member". type: channel, group or bot (bots the user owns, from BotFather).

name: list_members
label: Listing members
description: Members of a group or subscribers of a channel (channels only for admins) with each one's role, custom title, admin rights or restrictions, join date and who added them. filter: recent, admins, bots, restricted, banned, or search with query.

name: get_member
label: Checking a member
description: One member's role, rights or restrictions in a group or channel (user_id), and the chat's default permissions.

name: get_chat_permissions
label: Reading permissions
description: What ordinary members of a group may do (its default permissions), plus slow mode where known.

name: set_chat_permissions
label: Changing permissions
description: As an admin: changes what all members of a group may do. Needs approval.

name: promote_member
label: Changing an admin
description: As an admin with that right: makes a member an admin with the given rights, or demotes them back to a member with demote: true. title sets their member tag (the label by their name). Needs approval.

name: set_member_tag
label: Tagging a member
description: Sets or clears (empty tag) the member tag shown next to someone's name in a group — what used to be an admin's custom title, now for any member. Needs the right to manage tags. Read tags with get_members.

name: restrict_member
label: Restricting a member
description: As an admin: limits what one member may do (e.g. mute them with send_messages false) for days (0 = forever), or lifts restrictions with lift: true. Needs approval.

name: edit_chat_info
label: Editing chat info
description: As an admin: changes a group's or channel's title, description, or photo (photo: an attached image's name). Needs approval.

name: list_invite_links
label: Listing invite links
description: Invite links of a group or channel you admin, with their usage, limits and pending requests.

name: create_invite_link
label: Making an invite link
description: Creates an invite link: optional name, expiry in hours, member limit, and approval of joiners (requires_approval). revoke: an existing link to revoke instead. Needs approval.

name: list_join_requests
label: Checking join requests
description: People asking to join a group or channel you admin, with their bio and when they asked.

name: answer_join_request
label: Answering a join request
description: Approves or declines someone's request to join (user_id; approve true or false). Needs approval.

name: get_admin_log
label: Reading the admin log
description: Recent admin actions in a group or channel you admin (last 48 hours): edits, deletions, bans, joins, leaves, settings changes. query filters by text.

name: add_members
label: Adding members
description: Adds users (user_ids, e.g. contacts) to a group or channel. Needs approval.

name: create_chat
label: Creating a chat
description: Creates a new channel, group or forum group with a title and description, optionally adding user_ids. Needs approval.

name: join_chat
label: Joining a chat
description: Joins a public channel or group (chat_id or @username) or one by invite link (link). check_only: true just previews an invite link. Needs approval unless check_only.

name: list_blocked
label: Listing blocked accounts
description: Users, bots and chats the user has blocked, with ids for block_user (unblock).

name: add_contact
label: Adding a contact
description: Adds a user to contacts with a first and last name (user_id), or imports a phone number. share_phone: true shares the user's number with them. Needs approval.

name: set_draft
label: Saving a draft
description: Leaves a draft in a chat's message box (text, or empty to clear it) for the user to finish and send themselves. Nothing is sent.

name: start_bot
label: Starting a bot
description: Presses Start on a bot (bot user_id), with an optional start parameter from a deep link. Needs approval.

name: get_chat_stats
label: Reading statistics
description: Statistics of a channel or group you admin (Telegram offers them for bigger chats): members and growth, views, shares and reactions per post, top posters, recent post performance, and boost level.

name: get_post_stats
label: Reading post statistics
description: Views, shares and reactions of one channel post you admin (chat_id, message_id).

name: list_my_bots
label: Listing your bots
description: Bots the user owns, with user_id, username and whether the assistant can act as it (connect_bot).

name: get_bot_profile
label: Reading a bot profile
description: An owned bot's name, description (shown before Start) and short description (its bio).

name: edit_bot
label: Editing a bot
description: Changes an owned bot's name, description, short description (bio), or photo (an attached image's name in file). Needs approval.

name: create_bot
label: Creating a bot
description: Creates a new bot with a display name and a username ending in "bot". Its token is kept in the phone's secure storage (never shown) so connect: true lets the assistant drive it through the Bot API. Needs approval.

name: botfather
label: Talking to BotFather
description: Sends @BotFather a command and its follow-up answers in order, e.g. ["/setcommands", "@my_bot", "start - Begin\nhelp - Help"], ["/setinline", "@my_bot", "Search…"], ["/setjoingroups", "@my_bot", "Disable"], ["/mybots"]. Returns BotFather's replies. Deleting bots and revoking tokens are refused here. Needs approval.

name: delete_messages
label: Deleting messages
description: Deletes messages (message_ids) in a chat. for_everyone: true also removes them for the other people where Telegram allows it (your own messages, or any message as an admin). Can't be undone. Needs approval.

name: clear_chat_history
label: Clearing a chat
description: Deletes the whole message history of a chat for the user (for_everyone: true also for the other person in a private chat). The chat stays in the list. Can't be undone. Needs approval.

name: leave_chat
label: Leaving a chat
description: Leaves a group or unsubscribes from a channel. Needs approval.

name: delete_chat
label: Deleting a chat
description: Removes a chat entirely: for a private chat, deletes its history and removes it from the list; for a group or channel the user owns, deletes it for all members. Can't be undone. Needs approval.

name: block_user
label: Blocking
description: Blocks a user or bot (user_id), or unblocks them with unblock: true. Needs approval.

name: remove_contact
label: Removing a contact
description: Removes users (user_ids) from the user's contacts. Needs approval.

name: ban_member
label: Banning a member
description: As an admin: removes a member (user_id) from a group or channel. kick_only: true lets them rejoin later; otherwise they are banned (days: for how long, 0 = forever). delete_messages: true also deletes their messages. unban: true lifts a ban. Needs approval.

name: delete_all_from_member
label: Deleting a member's messages
description: As an admin of a group: deletes every message a member (user_id) sent there. Needs approval.

name: list_briefs
label: Opening briefs
description: The briefs written so far (morning, night and on demand), newest first, with brief_id values.

name: read_brief
label: Reading a brief
description: The full text of a brief (brief_id from list_briefs, or "latest").

name: write_brief
label: Writing a brief
description: Writes a new brief now, like "Brief me now" in the app: a priority-ordered rundown of what happened across Telegram and connected apps, following the user's brief settings. Read-only research; the brief is saved with the others and its full text comes back. Takes a minute or two. Use when the user asks for a brief, a catch-up or "what did I miss".

name: canvas_overview
label: Opening the Content Canvas
description: The Content Canvas: every folder (with folder_id, path and item count) and, with folder, the items in it (item_id, kind, chat, text, note). Use before organising things into it.

name: canvas_create_folder
label: Making a canvas folder
description: Creates a folder in the Content Canvas (or returns the existing one with that name), optionally inside parent (folder_id or name).

name: canvas_update_folder
label: Changing a canvas folder
description: Renames a canvas folder, changes its description, or moves it under parent ("" for the top).

name: canvas_export
label: Exporting a canvas folder
description: Exports a Content Canvas folder (and its subfolders unless subfolders: false) as json, md (Markdown), html or pdf. Returns the file's name; it appears in Files, and send_message can send it (files: [name]).

name: canvas_delete_folder
label: Deleting a canvas folder
description: Deletes a canvas folder and its subfolders (only the canvas, nothing in Telegram). Its items are deleted too unless move_items_to names another folder. Needs approval.

name: canvas_add
label: Saving to the canvas
description: Saves posts, DMs or comments into a canvas folder (made if missing), with an optional note on why. Pass refs, or chat_id with message_ids. Use one call per folder when classifying.

name: canvas_save
label: Saving to the canvas
description: Saves anything that isn't a Telegram message into a canvas folder (made if missing): a web link, an email, a file of this conversation, or an item from a connected app (a Notion page, Slack message, issue, task, calendar event, R2 file…). Give a title, its url and/or file, a short text (the gist or an excerpt), and source (e.g. "Gmail").

name: canvas_add_note
label: Writing a canvas note
description: Adds a text note (markdown) to a canvas folder, e.g. a summary of what the folder holds.

name: canvas_move
label: Moving canvas items
description: Moves canvas items (item_ids from canvas_overview) to another folder.

name: canvas_remove
label: Removing canvas items
description: Removes items (item_ids) from the canvas. Nothing in Telegram is touched.

name: create_reminder
label: Setting a reminder
description: Sets a reminder or a scheduled (cron) job. "Remind me to walk in 5 minutes" → text "Walk", in_minutes 5. "Remind me at 18:30" → at. Repeating: cron, five fields "minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week" in local time, e.g. "0 9 * * 1-5" weekdays at 9:00, "*/30 * * * *" every 30 minutes, "0 20 * * 0" Sundays at 20:00. A plain reminder is a phone notification that arrives on time even if the app is closed. Give prompt to make it a job: at that time you run the prompt (e.g. "summarise my unread channels", "send Liya good morning") and your answer becomes the notification.

name: list_reminders
label: Listing reminders
description: The user's reminders and scheduled jobs: what they say, when they fire next, how they repeat.

name: update_reminder
label: Changing a reminder
description: Changes a reminder or job: its text, time (in_minutes / at), cron schedule, prompt, or turns it on/off. Pass cron "" to make a repeating one fire just once at the new time.

name: delete_reminder
label: Removing a reminder
description: Removes a reminder or scheduled job for good.

name: zip_files
label: Zipping files
description: Packs files of this conversation (attachments, generated or downloaded files) into one .zip, which then is a file of this conversation too: send it with send_message. Use when asked to zip or compress files, or to send many files as one.

name: vault_list
label: Checking the vault
description: Lists what the user keeps in their vault: their own phone numbers, emails, addresses, ID and document numbers, work and other personal details, with each item's id. Sensitive values are masked; read one with vault_get. Use it when you need a detail about the user (e.g. their address for a delivery form).

name: vault_get
label: Reading from the vault
description: Reads one vault item with its full value, by item_id or by what it is ("work phone", "passport"). Sensitive items are withheld in runs that read other people's messages, emails or pages, and in watch runs.

name: vault_save
label: Saving to the vault
description: Adds an item to the user's vault, or changes one (give item_id). Use when the user tells you a personal detail to keep ("my work number is …", "save my passport number"). Mark ID numbers, account numbers and health details sensitive. Never store passwords, PINs, card numbers or security codes.

name: vault_delete
label: Removing from the vault
description: Removes an item from the user's vault, when they ask you to or it is no longer true.

name: list_routines
label: Listing routines
description: The user's routines: named lists of steps (ask the assistant, run a tool, notify, wait, conditions) that run by hand, on a schedule or on a phone event, with their last results.

name: run_routine
label: Running a routine
description: Runs one of the user's routines now and returns what each step did.

name: create_routine
label: Building a routine
description: Builds a routine the user can see and edit under Settings → Routines. Steps run in order; text in steps may use {{last}} (previous step's result), {{step2}}, {{trigger}}, {{date}}, {{time}} and {{vault:Label}}. Kinds: ask (prompt: an instruction for the assistant), tool (tool + args: one tool with fixed inputs, no AI; not for tools that delete or spend), notify (title, body), wait (seconds), condition (test: contains, not_contains, is_empty, not_empty, succeeded or failed; value; otherwise: stop or skip_next). Triggers: manual, daily (at "HH:MM", days 1 Monday … 7 Sunday), interval (every_minutes, 15 or more) or phone (phone_event and its details).

name: update_routine
label: Changing a routine
description: Turns a routine on or off, or renames it. For bigger changes the user edits it in Settings → Routines, or you make a new one.

name: delete_routine
label: Removing a routine
description: Removes a routine for good.

name: fetch_url
label: Reading a web page
description: Reads a web page or file over HTTP without running its scripts: title, readable text, links, forms and the page's script files. Fast; best for blogs, articles, docs, JSON APIs and plain sites (e.g. "what blogs are on dagmawibabi.com/blog": fetch it, then fetch the posts you need from the links). Use find to get only the parts mentioning something; raw for the exact source (JavaScript, JSON, HTML) e.g. to look for the API a script calls. If the text is nearly empty the site is a script app: use browser_open instead.

name: http_request
label: Calling a web API
description: Sends any HTTP request (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE…) with headers and a JSON, form or raw body, and returns the status, headers and body. For APIs and webhooks. Cookies from earlier fetch_url calls to the same site are sent along. The user approves it first. For reading pages use fetch_url instead.

name: submit_form
label: Submitting a web form
description: Fills in and submits a form on a plain HTML page (one fetch_url listed under forms): hidden fields and defaults are kept, the values you give are set, and the result page is returned. The user approves it first. Forms run by scripts need the browser tools instead.

name: download_file
label: Downloading a file
description: Downloads a file from the web onto the phone. It then counts as a file of this conversation: send it to a chat by passing its name in files, zip it, or look at it with view_image if it is a picture.

name: browser_open
label: Opening in the browser
description: Opens a page in the assistant's real browser, which runs the page's JavaScript like Chrome does. Returns the page's text and its usable elements, numbered (links, buttons, text fields, selects). Then use browser_type to fill fields, browser_click to press buttons, browser_read to read again. Use it for sites that are apps (JavaScript-heavy web apps, forms, anything fetch_url shows empty), and to follow a link (open its href; no approval needed). The user can watch it live in the app's Browser screen.

name: browser_read
label: Reading the browser page
description: Reads the page open in the browser again, after it changed: text (from offset), or only what mentions find, and freshly numbered elements. Numbers from an earlier read may have changed.

name: browser_type
label: Typing in the browser
description: Types text into a field of the open page (element number from the last browser_open/browser_read), or picks an option of a select by its text. Replaces what is there unless append is true. Nothing is sent until a button is clicked (browser_click) or the field is submitted (browser_submit).

name: browser_click
label: Clicking in the browser
description: Clicks an element of the open page (a button, link, checkbox, tab) by its number, waits for the page to react and returns it. Clicks can send or buy things, so the user approves each one. To just follow a link, browser_open its href instead.

name: browser_submit
label: Submitting in the browser
description: Presses Enter in a field of the open page and submits its form, e.g. a search box. The user approves it first.

name: browser_back
label: Going back
description: Goes back to the previous page in the browser and reads it.

name: browser_run_js
label: Running a script on the page
description: Runs JavaScript in the open page and returns the value of its last expression (as JSON). For reading what the other tools miss (document.querySelectorAll(...)) or doing what they can't. The user approves it first.

name: get_star_balance
label: Checking your Stars
description: The user's Telegram Stars balance, plus how many Stars their active subscriptions need and the prices for buying more (buying happens in Telegram's official app).

name: list_star_transactions
label: Reading Star history
description: The user's Star transactions, newest first: Stars bought, received from people, spent on reactions, paid media, subscriptions, bots and gifts, with who was on the other side.

name: send_star_reaction
label: Sending Stars
description: Gives Stars to a post or message as a paid ⭐ reaction (from 1 to 2500 Stars); the Stars go to the channel or chat's owner and the user shows up among its top supporters unless anonymous. This is how to "star" a post or a person's content. Spends the user's Stars, so the user approves it every time.

name: get_star_reactors
label: Seeing who sent Stars
description: Who gave Stars to a post or message, the top supporters first, and how many in total.

name: list_star_subscriptions
label: Listing Star subscriptions
description: The channels and groups the user pays Stars for each month, with price, renewal date and status.

name: set_star_subscription
label: Changing a Star subscription
description: Cancels a Star subscription (it runs until the paid period ends) or turns a cancelled one back on. Needs approval.

name: get_star_revenue
label: Checking Star earnings
description: Stars earned by one of the user's channels or bots (chat_id of the channel, or of the bot's chat): total, available to withdraw, and their value in USD.

name: web_screenshot
label: Taking a screenshot
description: Takes a screenshot (PNG) of a web page with the second browser engine: the phone-sized screen, or the whole page with full_page. Without url it shoots the page open in the main browser (browser_open). The picture is shown to the user, you can look at it with view_image, and it can be sent to a chat with send_message. Use when the user wants to see a page, or when a page is easier to understand by looking.

name: web_inspect
label: Inspecting a page
description: Opens a page in the second browser engine and returns what a developer would check: console messages and errors, the network requests it made (APIs it calls), its cookie names, and the HTML after its scripts ran. Without url it inspects the main browser's page. Good for finding the API behind a web app or why a page fails.

name: web_run_async_js
label: Running a page script
description: Runs JavaScript in a page in the second browser engine as an async function body: it may await (fetch the site's own API with its cookies, wait for elements), and its return value comes back as JSON. Without url, uses the main browser's page. The user approves it first.

name: run_code
label: Running code
description: Runs code in a sandbox on the phone, cut off from the app and Telegram: Python (Pyodide: the standard library plus numpy, pandas, matplotlib, pillow and other packages it loads from imports; first use downloads Python) or JavaScript. Use it to calculate, analyse data, convert files, make charts, images, CSV/JSON/text files. Pass files (names from this conversation) to give the code input files: in Python they are in the working directory, in JavaScript files["name"] is a Uint8Array. To produce files, Python writes them into the out/ folder (e.g. plt.savefig("out/chart.png")); JavaScript sets outFiles["name"] = string or Uint8Array. Produced files are shown to the user and can be sent with send_message. Printed output comes back, and the value of the last expression (Python) or of return (JavaScript runs as an async function body).

name: github_repo
label: Looking at a GitHub repo
description: A public GitHub repository at a glance: description, stars, forks, open issues, languages, topics, licence, default branch, latest activity and the start of its README. repo is "owner/name" or any github.com URL.

name: github_list
label: Browsing a GitHub repo
description: Lists the files and folders at a path of a public repo (the root when path is missing), on a branch, tag or commit (ref).

name: github_read
label: Reading a file on GitHub
description: Reads a file from a public repo: repo + path (+ ref), or a github.com/…/blob/… URL in repo. Long files read in parts with offset; find returns only the lines around a word.

name: github_search
label: Searching GitHub
description: Searches public GitHub: repositories (e.g. "flutter telegram client stars:>50"), issues and pull requests (e.g. "repo:owner/name crash is:open"), or users. Uses GitHub's search syntax.

name: github_issues
label: Reading GitHub issues
description: Issues or pull requests of a public repo (open, closed or all), or one of them in full with its comments (number).

name: github_commits
label: Reading GitHub commits
description: Recent commits of a public repo, optionally only those touching path, on a branch (ref); or one commit in full (sha) with its changed files.

name: github_releases
label: Reading GitHub releases
description: Releases of a public repo, newest first, with their notes and downloadable assets (APKs, binaries) and download counts.

name: github_download
label: Downloading from GitHub
description: Downloads from a public repo onto the phone: the whole repo as a .zip (at ref), one file (path), or a release asset (asset_url from github_releases). It becomes a file of this conversation, ready for send_message or run_code.

name: list_stories
label: Listing stories
description: Stories of a person or channel (chat_id; the user's own when missing): the active ones (last 24-48 h), the ones kept on the profile, and for the user's own also the archive. Each with story_id, date, caption, views and reactions where Telegram shows them.

name: view_story
label: Viewing a story
description: One story in full: caption, photo or video, privacy, views, reactions and forwards. The picture (or a video's first frame) is shown to the user and can be looked at with view_image. Viewing marks it seen, as in Telegram, unless peek is true.

name: story_viewers
label: Seeing who viewed a story
description: Who viewed one of the user's own stories (or a channel's they admin), who reacted with what, and who forwarded or reposted it.

name: post_story
label: Posting a story
description: Posts a photo or video (up to 60 s) as a story, from a file of this conversation, with an optional caption. Privacy: everyone, contacts, close_friends or selected (user_ids). active_hours 6, 12, 24 or 48 (6/12/48 need Premium). keep_on_profile keeps it on the profile after it expires. chat_id posts for a channel the user can post stories in. The user approves it first.

name: edit_story
label: Editing a story
description: Changes one of the user's stories: its caption, its photo/video (files), its privacy, or whether it stays on the profile. Needs approval.

name: delete_story
label: Deleting a story
description: Deletes one of the user's stories (or a channel's they manage) for everyone. Can't be undone.

name: react_to_story
label: Reacting to a story
description: Puts an emoji reaction on someone's story, or removes the user's reaction (emoji empty). Needs approval.

name: get_folder
label: Reading a folder
description: A chat folder's full rules: its name, icon, the chats included, excluded and pinned, and the chat types it takes in.

name: create_folder
label: Creating a folder
description: Creates a Telegram chat folder: a name, chats to include (chat_ids), and/or whole types (contacts, non_contacts, bots, groups, channels), chats to exclude, and filters (exclude_muted, exclude_read, exclude_archived). icon: All, Unread, Unmuted, Bots, Channels, Groups, Private, Custom, Setup, Cat, Crown, Favorite, Flower, Game, Home, Love, Mask, Party, Sport, Study, Trade, Travel, Work. Needs approval.

name: edit_folder
label: Editing a folder
description: Changes a chat folder: rename, change icon, add_chat_ids / remove_chat_ids, pin chats, change the included types or filters. Unmentioned settings stay. Needs approval.

name: delete_folder
label: Deleting a folder
description: Deletes a chat folder. The chats themselves stay. Needs approval.

name: reorder_folders
label: Reordering folders
description: Puts the chat folders in a new order (all folder_ids, first to last). Needs approval.

name: suggested_folders
label: Getting folder ideas
description: Folders Telegram suggests for this account (e.g. "Unread", "Personal"), ready to create with create_folder.

name: share_folder
label: Sharing a folder
description: Makes an invite link to a folder so others can add it with its chats (groups and channels only), or lists its existing links (list: true). Needs approval to make one.

name: set_chat_settings
label: Changing chat settings
description: Changes how a chat works (as its admin, or for a private chat where it applies): auto_delete (seconds: 0 off, 86400 a day, 604800 a week, 2678400 a month), slow_mode (seconds between messages: 0, 10, 30, 60, 300, 900, 3600), protect_content (no forwarding or saving), history_for_new_members, join_by_request, join_to_send (must join to write in a discussion group), sign_messages and show_author (channels), hide_members, aggressive_antispam, translatable, username (public link; empty makes it private), discussion_chat_id (link a channel's comments group; 0 unlinks). Only the given ones change. Needs approval.

name: set_chat_reactions
label: Changing allowed reactions
description: Which reactions members may use in a group or channel the user admins: all, some (emojis), or none. Needs approval.

name: manage_topic
label: Managing a topic
description: In a group with topics: create one (name, no topic_id), or change one (topic_id): rename, close or reopen (closed), pin or unpin (pinned). Needs approval.

name: delete_topic
label: Deleting a topic
description: Deletes a topic of a group with all its messages. Can't be undone.

name: get_boosts
label: Checking boosts
description: A channel's or group's boost level, how many boosts it has and needs for the next level, Premium members, and (for admins) who boosted it.

name: invite_link_joins
label: Seeing who joined by a link
description: Who joined a group or channel through one of its invite links (from list_invite_links), and when.

name: list_sessions
label: Checking logged-in devices
description: Every device and app logged in to the account: app and version, whether it is an official Telegram app, device, system, IP and location, when it logged in and was last active, which one is this phone, and the auto-logout period for inactive devices.

name: end_session
label: Logging a device out
description: Logs one device out of the account (session_id from list_sessions), or every device except this phone (all_others). Use when the user doesn't recognise a device. Always asks first.

name: set_session_options
label: Changing device settings
description: Sets after how many days of inactivity devices are logged out (7, 30, 90, 180 or 365), and/or whether one device (session_id) may take calls. Needs approval.

name: get_privacy
label: Checking privacy
description: The account's privacy settings: who sees last seen, profile photo, phone number, bio and birthday; who may add the user to groups and call them; whether read times are shown; whether strangers may start chats. Each with the people added as exceptions.

name: set_privacy
label: Changing privacy
description: Changes one privacy setting: setting is last_seen, profile_photo, phone_number, bio, birthdate, invites, calls, p2p_calls, read_dates (show_read_dates) or new_chats (allow strangers). audience: everybody, contacts or nobody; always_user_ids and never_user_ids are exceptions. Needs approval.

name: get_profile
label: Reading your profile
description: The user's own profile: name, username, bio, birthday, phone, Premium, and their personal channel.

name: edit_profile
label: Editing your profile
description: Changes the user's profile: first_name/last_name, bio (70 characters, more with Premium), username (empty removes it), birthday ("YYYY-MM-DD" or "MM-DD"; "" removes it), a new profile photo from files, or the personal channel shown on the profile (personal_channel_id; 0 removes). Only given fields change. Needs approval.

name: account_health
label: Checking account security
description: A security check-up of the account: two-step verification and its recovery email, devices logged in (unknown, unofficial or long-idle ones), who can see the phone number and who can add the user to groups, and the account's self-destruct period, with a score and what to fix.

name: open_telegram_link
label: Opening a Telegram link
description: Works out what a Telegram link is and opens it for you: t.me/username (a chat, channel, bot or person: its chat_id and details), t.me/channel/123 and t.me/c/… (that message, readable straight away), invite links t.me/+… (the chat, its size and description, without joining), stories, sticker sets, folder links, bot start links and others. Use the returned chat_id with the other tools (read_messages, join_chat…).

name: search_all_chats
label: Searching every chat
description: Searches all the user's chats at once (or one chat, a folder, or the archive) for a kind of content: photos, videos, files, links, music, voice messages, video messages, GIFs, or any message, optionally matching query and between dates. E.g. "every PDF people sent me last month" (type files, query "pdf", since_days 31). Results are newest first; pass next_offset for more.

name: inline_bot_query
label: Asking an inline bot
description: Asks an inline bot (@gif, @vid, @wiki, @bing, @pic, @sticker, @youtube, @music, any bot with inline mode) for results for a query, as typing "@bot query" in Telegram does. Returns numbered results; send one with send_inline_result.

name: send_inline_result
label: Sending an inline result
description: Sends one result from inline_bot_query to a chat, as if picked from the inline list. Needs approval.

name: list_message_effects
label: Listing message effects
description: The animated effects a message can be sent with in private chats (🔥 👍 ❤️ 🎉 💩 and more): effect_id and emoji, and which need Premium. Pass effect_id to send_message to use one.

name: reactions_to_me
label: Checking reactions to your messages
description: Reactions people put on the user's messages: by default the new (unseen) ones across all chats, with who reacted with what on which message; with chat_id and all, every reaction on the user's recent messages in that chat.

name: mark_reactions_seen
label: Marking reactions seen
description: Marks the new reactions to the user's messages as seen, in one chat or (no chat_id) in every chat. Needs approval.

name: video_chat
label: Checking a video chat
description: Whether a group or channel has a video chat (group call or live stream) going or scheduled: its title, how many are in it, who is speaking, whether the user can manage it. One-to-one calls can't be placed from this app; list_calls shows their history.

name: manage_video_chat
label: Managing a video chat
description: As admin of a group or channel: start a video chat (now, or scheduled with start_at; live_stream for an RTMP stream), end it, rename it (title), invite user_ids, get an invite link, or mute/unmute new participants. Needs approval.

name: storage_report
label: Checking storage
description: How much space Telegram's files take on this phone, in total, by kind (photos, videos, music…) and by chat (the biggest first), plus its database.

name: clean_storage
label: Clearing cached files
description: Frees space by deleting cached Telegram files on this phone (they stay in Telegram and download again when opened): only older_than_days, only some kinds (photos, videos, files, music, voice, video_messages, gifs, stickers), only some chats, or until the cache is under keep_mb. Needs approval.

name: data_usage
label: Checking data use
description: How much mobile data, Wi-Fi and roaming Telegram used on this phone since the counters were last reset, by kind (photos, videos, files, calls…). reset: true starts the counters again (needs approval through the app).

name: search_books
label: Searching books
description: Searches books by title, author, subject or anything (query), across Open Library (millions of books: editions, ratings, covers, which are free to read), Project Gutenberg and Standard Ebooks (public-domain ebooks, free to download), and Google Books. free_only keeps books with a legal free copy. Each result has a book_id for book_details and download_book.

name: book_details
label: Reading about a book
description: Everything about one book (book_id from search_books): description, authors, first published, subjects, editions and ISBNs, pages, ratings, the formats it can be downloaded in when it is free, and its cover, which is shown to the user.

name: find_free_copy
label: Looking for a free copy
description: Checks every legal source for a free copy of a book (public domain or openly licensed): Gutenberg, Standard Ebooks, and Internet Archive scans. Says plainly when there is none (most books still under copyright) and where it can be borrowed or bought instead.

name: download_book
label: Downloading a book
description: Downloads a free, legal ebook (book_id from search_books or find_free_copy) onto the phone: epub (default), kindle, pdf or txt where offered. It becomes a file of this conversation: send it with send_message, or read it with run_code. Only public-domain and openly licensed books can be downloaded.

name: x_post
label: Reading a post on X
description: One post on X (Twitter) from its link or id: text, author, date, likes, reposts, replies, views, its photos and videos (the first photo is shown), and the post it quotes. Works without an X account.

name: x_profile
label: Looking at an X profile
description: An X (Twitter) profile: name, bio, followers, following, posts count, joined date, location, website and picture. Recent posts, search and posting need the user signed in to x.com in the app's browser (then use browser_open on x.com).

name: youtube_search
label: Searching YouTube
description: Searches YouTube for videos (or channels or playlists with type). With the YouTube key: sort by relevance, date, views or rating; filter by length, how recent, country, captions, or live now. Videos come with title, channel, length, views, likes, comments, published date, thumbnail and link.

name: youtube_video
label: Reading a YouTube video
description: A YouTube video's details (link or id): title, channel, published date, length, exact views, likes and comment count (with the key), category, tags, topics, quality, captions, the full description and chapters, where it is blocked, and its thumbnail (shown to the user).

name: youtube_transcript
label: Reading a transcript
description: The captions of a YouTube video as text with timestamps, in a language when given. YouTube often refuses apps without a signed-in browser; then the tool says so, and the description and chapters are what there is.

name: youtube_channel
label: Looking at a YouTube channel
description: A YouTube channel (@handle, link, id or name): description, subscribers, total views, videos, average views per video, country, when it started, and its latest uploads with their views.

name: youtube_playlist
label: Reading a YouTube playlist
description: The videos of a YouTube playlist (link or id) with views and lengths, and, with the key, every video (up to 200) and the total running time.

name: youtube_comments
label: Reading YouTube comments
description: Comments on a YouTube video: the top ones (or newest), each with author, likes, date and a few replies, or only those containing words. Use it for "what do people think of this video". Needs the YouTube key.

name: youtube_trending
label: Checking what's trending on YouTube
description: The most popular videos on YouTube right now in a country, optionally one category (music, gaming, news, sports, comedy, entertainment, education, science, film, howto, people). YouTube has no chart for some countries (Ethiopia among them); use a nearby one like KE or US. Needs the YouTube key.

name: youtube_live
label: Finding live streams
description: Live streams on YouTube now (with how many are watching), or upcoming premieres and streams with their start times: about a topic, or from one channel. Needs the YouTube key.

name: youtube_channel_videos
label: Listing a channel's videos
description: A YouTube channel's videos with views, likes and comments: its latest uploads (default) or its most viewed, plus how often it uploads and its average views. Needs the YouTube key.

name: youtube_compare_channels
label: Comparing YouTube channels
description: Puts 2-6 YouTube channels side by side: subscribers, total views, videos, average views per video and age. Needs the YouTube key.

name: youtube_new_uploads
label: Checking new uploads
description: New videos from the given channels in the last hours, newest first. Cheap (about 2 quota units per channel), so it suits a schedule watch: "every 2 hours, tell me when MKBHD or Veritasium uploads". Needs the YouTube key.

name: send_rich_message
label: Sending a rich message
description: Sends a rich message laid out in blocks: # headings, paragraphs, - bullet / 1. numbered / - [ ] checkbox lists (nest by indenting), | tables | with :--: alignment, > quotes (a last "— Name" line is the credit), ``` code ```, $$ math $$ and inline $math$, --- dividers, <details><summary>Title</summary> … </details> collapsibles, and ![caption](file) for an attached photo, video, GIF, audio or file. Inline: **bold**, _italic_, __underline__, ~~strike~~, ||spoiler||, ==highlight==, `code`, [text](url), ^sup^, ~sub~. Use it for tables, reports and structured answers; plain chat goes through send_message. Some features may need Telegram Premium. Needs approval.

name: edit_rich_message
label: Editing a rich message
description: Replaces the text of one of the user's messages with a rich message written in the same Markdown as send_rich_message (no new media). Needs approval.

name: read_rich_message
label: Reading a rich message
description: The whole of a rich message as Markdown (tables, headings, lists…). Messages lists show long ones cut short; this loads the rest.

name: list_channel_dms
label: Reading channel DMs
description: For a channel the user administers (or its direct-messages group): the people who messaged the channel, one conversation (topic) each, with unread counts and the last message. Read one with read_channel_dm; answer with reply_channel_dm.

name: read_channel_dm
label: Reading a channel DM
description: Messages of one channel direct-messages conversation (topic_id from list_channel_dms), newest first.

name: reply_channel_dm
label: Answering a channel DM
description: Answers someone in a channel's direct messages as the channel. Text, or attached files. Needs approval.

name: set_channel_dms
label: Changing channel DMs
description: Turns a channel's direct messages on or off (as its owner or an admin), optionally charging star_price Stars per message (0 = free). Needs approval.

name: get_profile_music
label: Reading profile music
description: The songs on someone's profile (or the user's own with no user_id): title, performer, length and file_id. send_message can't forward them; mention them instead.

name: add_profile_music
label: Adding profile music
description: Adds an attached audio file (mp3, m4a…) to the user's own profile music. Needs approval.

name: remove_profile_music
label: Removing profile music
description: Removes a song (file_id from get_profile_music) from the user's profile. Needs approval.

name: list_welcome_messages
label: Reading welcome messages
description: The welcome messages a group or channel sends people who join (needs the admin right to send welcome messages), with their ids.

name: set_welcome_message
label: Setting a welcome message
description: Adds a welcome message to a group or channel, or replaces one with welcome_message_id. text may be Markdown like send_rich_message (sent as a rich message when it has headings, tables or lists); one attached photo, video or file goes with it. Needs approval.

name: delete_welcome_message
label: Deleting a welcome message
description: Deletes one welcome message (or all with all: true) from a group or channel. Needs approval.

name: message_read_status
label: Checking if it was read
description: Whether messages the user sent were read. In a private chat: read or not, and when (if neither side hides read times and it was sent in the last week). In a group: who viewed it (small groups, recent messages). In a channel: the view count. Without message_id it checks the user's last few messages in the chat. Telegram never says whether someone merely opened the chat.

name: get_replied_message
label: Following a reply
description: The message another one replies to or quotes (in the same chat or another one), with the quoted part. Use it to understand a reply in context; its ref opens the original. follow: n walks up a reply chain up to n steps (default 1, max 10).

name: view_profile_photo
label: Looking at a profile photo
description: Lets you see someone's profile picture (user_id), or a group's or channel's photo (chat_id), with your own eyes; count > 1 also shows their earlier profile pictures (users only, up to 6). The pictures come right after the result, and the user sees them too.

name: set_private_note
label: Saving a private note
description: Saves a private note on a contact's profile that only the user sees in Telegram (e.g. "met at the conference, likes chess"). Empty note clears it. Supports **bold**, _italic_, __underline__, ~~strike~~ and ||spoiler||. Read notes with get_private_note or get_chat_info.

name: get_private_note
label: Reading a private note
description: The user's private Telegram note on a contact, if any.

name: send_ephemeral_command
label: Sending a private bot command
description: Sends a bot one of its ephemeral commands in a chat: only that bot receives it, and its answer is visible only to the user (others in a group see nothing). Only commands the bot marks as ephemeral work (get_bot_commands shows them). Needs approval.

name: get_bot_commands
label: Reading bot commands
description: A bot's commands with descriptions, and which are ephemeral (answered privately).

name: stop_bot_reply
label: Stopping a bot reply
description: Stops a bot (an AI bot, usually) that is still writing its answer in a chat, keeping or dropping what it wrote as the bot decides.

name: connect_bot
label: Connecting a bot
description: Lets the assistant act as one of the user's own bots: fetches its token from @BotFather and keeps it in the phone's secure storage (never shown). Then bot_api and stream_bot_message work with it. disconnect: true forgets it. Needs approval.

name: bot_api
label: Using the Bot API
description: Calls a Telegram Bot API method as a connected bot (connect_bot first), e.g. getMe, getUpdates, sendMessage {chat_id, text}, setMyCommands {commands: [{command, description}]}, setMyDescription, setChatMenuButton, getChat, sendPhoto with a URL, answerCallbackQuery, sendMessageDraft. params is the method's JSON body. Reading methods (get…) run without asking; everything else needs approval.

name: stream_bot_message
label: Streaming a bot message
description: Has a connected bot write a message to someone live, the way AI bots do: the text appears word by word as a draft (sendMessageDraft), then lands as a real message. chat_id is the private chat with the person (their user id); defaults to the user themself. Needs approval.

name: music_search
label: Searching music
description: Finds songs, albums or artists (Apple Music catalogue, no account): title, artist, album, year, genre, length, artwork, a 30-second preview, and YouTube Music / Spotify links (the user is on Android: share those, not Apple Music links). type: song (default), album or artist. The user sees cards they can tap and play.

name: music_album
label: Opening an album
description: An album's tracks (with previews), release date, genre, label and artwork. album_id from music_search.

name: music_artist
label: Looking up an artist
description: An artist: a short biography (Wikipedia), where they're from, active years, genres (MusicBrainz) and their albums, newest first. Give artist_id from music_search, or name.

name: movie_search
label: Searching movies
description: Finds films: title, year, director, genres, length and poster (Wikidata and Wikipedia, no account). For TV series use tv_search.

name: movie_details
label: Looking up a movie
description: One film in full: Wikipedia summary, director, writers, main cast, release date, genres, runtime, country, language, age rating, budget and box office when known, poster, trailer and IMDb link. movie_id (like "Q25188") from movie_search.

name: tv_search
label: Searching TV shows
description: Finds TV series (TVmaze): network, years, status, genres, rating, poster and summary.

name: tv_show
label: Looking up a TV show
description: A TV series in full: summary, seasons (episode counts and dates), main cast, the next episode if it is still airing, and with season set, that season's episodes. show_id from tv_search.

name: crypto_prices
label: Checking crypto prices
description: Live crypto prices (CoinGecko): price, 1h/24h/7d change, market cap and rank, 24h volume, high/low, all-time high and a 7-day sparkline. coins: names, symbols or CoinGecko ids ("bitcoin", "ETH", "solana"); leave it out for the top coins by market cap. vs: quote currency (usd default; eur, gbp, btc…). The user sees a card.

name: crypto_coin
label: Looking up a coin
description: One cryptocurrency in full (CoinGecko): description, price and changes, market cap, supply (circulating, total, max), all-time high/low, categories, homepage and a price chart over days (1, 7, 30, 90, 365).

name: crypto_trending
label: Finding trending coins
description: The coins most searched on CoinGecko in the last 24 hours, with price and 24h change.

name: stock_quote
label: Checking stock prices
description: Stock, ETF, index, futures or forex quotes (Yahoo Finance, may be delayed): price, change, day range, 52-week range, previous close, exchange, currency and a price chart. symbols: tickers like AAPL, MSFT, ^GSPC (S&P 500), BTC-USD, EURUSD=X, 7203.T; use stock_search to find one. range: 1d, 5d, 1mo (default), 6mo, 1y, 5y.

name: stock_search
label: Finding a ticker
description: Finds ticker symbols by company or fund name (Yahoo Finance): symbol, name, exchange and type.

name: currency_convert
label: Converting currency
description: Converts money between currencies at European Central Bank reference rates (Frankfurter; updated on working days). amount (default 1), from (USD), to: one or more ISO codes. date: a past day (YYYY-MM-DD). days: also returns the rate history for the first "to" currency over that many days (up to 365), for a chart.

name: weather
label: Checking the weather
description: Current weather and a forecast (Open-Meteo): temperature, feels-like, humidity, wind, conditions, the next 24 hours and up to 14 days (highs, lows, rain chance, sunrise, sunset). place: a city or town; or latitude and longitude. units: metric (default) or imperial.

name: flight_status
label: Tracking a flight
description: A flight's route and, if it is in the air now, its live position, altitude, speed, aircraft and registration (adsbdb and adsb.lol, from ADS-B receivers; schedules and delays aren't available). flight: the flight number as on the ticket (BA117, UA 901) or the ICAO callsign (BAW117).

name: flight_search
label: Finding flights
description: Builds ready-to-open searches on Google Flights, Skyscanner and Kayak for a trip (no free service gives fares, so prices show when the user opens one). from and to: airport or city IATA codes (LHR, NYC); date and return_date: YYYY-MM-DD; adults (default 1); cabin: economy, premium, business or first.

name: public_holidays
label: Looking up holidays
description: Public holidays in a country for a year (Nager.Date): date, local and English name, and whether it is nationwide. country: two-letter code (US, GB, ET, DE). Upcoming ones are marked, and the next one has next: true. One call is enough: without a year, when few are left this year the result already includes the first ones of next year (includes_next_year). Call again only for a different country or a specific other year.

name: reddit_posts
label: Reading Reddit
description: Posts from a subreddit, or Reddit's front page (r/popular): title, author, score, comment count, flair, link, picture and the start of the text. sort: hot (default), new, top, rising; time for top: hour, day, week, month, year, all. The user sees cards; reddit_post opens one with its comments.

name: reddit_search
label: Searching Reddit
description: Searches Reddit posts, everywhere or in one subreddit. sort: relevance (default), hot, top, new, comments.

name: reddit_post
label: Opening a Reddit post
description: One Reddit post with its full text and top comments (with replies), by link or post id.

name: reddit_subreddit
label: Looking up a subreddit
description: About a subreddit: title, description, members, online now, created, icon and banner.

name: hn_stories
label: Reading Hacker News
description: Hacker News stories: top (default), new, best, ask (Ask HN), show (Show HN) or job. Each with title, link, site, points, author, comment count and age. The user sees cards; hn_item opens one with its comments.

name: hn_search
label: Searching Hacker News
description: Searches Hacker News stories or comments (Algolia). sort: relevance (default) or date.

name: hn_item
label: Opening a Hacker News thread
description: One Hacker News story (or comment) with its text and comment tree, by id or news.ycombinator.com link.

name: hn_user
label: Looking up a Hacker News user
description: A Hacker News user: karma, when they joined, about text, and their latest submissions.

name: bible_passage
label: Reading the Bible
description: Bible text from YouVersion for a reference: one verse, a range or a whole chapter ("John 3:16", "1 Cor 13:4-7", "Psalm 23", "Rom 8:28-9:2"). version: an abbreviation like KJV, NIV, ESV, AMP, or a version_id; default the user's version (Settings → Bible). The user sees a verse card. Quote the text exactly; never invent scripture.

name: bible_chapter
label: Opening a chapter
description: A whole Bible chapter to read, with section headings, and what comes before and after. The user sees a reader card they can page through.

name: bible_compare
label: Comparing translations
description: The same passage in several Bible versions side by side, e.g. John 1:1 in KJV, NIV and ESV.

name: bible_verse_of_the_day
label: Finding the verse of the day
description: YouVersion's verse of the day (with its artwork when there is some), today's or another date's, in the user's version.

name: bible_versions
label: Listing Bible versions
description: Bible versions (translations) in a language: id, abbreviation, title, books, copyright. By default only the versions the user's YouVersion app may read; include_unlicensed lists every version (marked licensed: false, such as NIV until its license is accepted on platform.youversion.com). language: en, am, es, fr, or * for all.

name: bible_search
label: Searching the Bible
description: Finds verses about a topic or containing words ("love your enemies", "anxiety", "faith hope love"), in a version, with their text. The user sees result cards.

name: bible_books
label: Listing the books
description: The books in a Bible version with their chapter counts, Old and New Testament.

name: finance_sync_sms
label: Reading bank texts
description: Reads the phone's SMS inbox and turns bank and wallet messages (CBE, Awash, BOA, Dashen, Zemen, Telebirr, NIB, M-Pesa, Amhara, Ahadu, Berhan, Hibret, Apollo, CBE Birr) into transactions with Totals' parser: amount, fees, balance after, counterparty, reference and receipt link, de-duplicated by reference. Account balances follow the newest message. Accounts named in messages but not added yet are created (detected: true) unless create_accounts is false. By default reads from the last sync, or 180 days back the first time. Run it before answering about money when the last sync is old. The user sees a sync card.

name: finance_parse_sms
label: Reading a bank message
description: Parses one bank SMS the user pasted or forwarded, without saving it: bank, CREDIT/DEBIT, amount, fees, balance after, account, counterparty, reference, receipt link. With save true it is recorded as a transaction like a synced one.

name: finance_overview
label: Checking your money
description: The complete picture in one dashboard: total balance, every account, this period's income, spending and net with a daily chart, top categories, budgets and the latest transactions. Only for broad asks like "how am I doing" or "give me the full picture"; for one thing (a balance, an account, spending, transactions) use the tool for that instead. The user sees a dashboard card.

name: finance_accounts
label: Listing accounts
description: Account balances. With account_id (or bank) only that account: its card, balance, when it was last reported and this month's in and out. Without, every account and the total. "How much is in my CBE?" is account_id "CBE"; "what are my balances?" is no filter. The user sees account cards for exactly what is returned.

name: finance_add_account
label: Adding an account
description: Adds a bank account, wallet or cash pocket. bank: a bank from finance_banks (name, short name or id), "Cash", or "Other". number: the full account number, or the phone number for wallets like Telebirr; the last digits are what match bank SMS. Transactions from that bank waiting for an account move onto it.

name: finance_update_account
label: Updating an account
description: Changes an account: nickname, number, holder, balance (a manual correction), whether it counts in totals, dormant, default.

name: finance_delete_account
label: Removing an account
description: Removes an account. Its transactions stay (without an account) unless delete_transactions is true. The user approves first.

name: finance_transactions
label: Looking at transactions
description: Transaction history, newest first, filtered by account, bank, type, category, counterparty or note words, amount range and dates, with the matching totals. Filter to what was asked: "my spending at Shoa" is type expense and query Shoa; "CBE transactions" is account_id CBE. The user sees just that list. Use ids from here to update or delete one.

name: finance_add_transaction
label: Recording a transaction
