description: A word's pronunciation (with audio), meanings by part of speech, examples, synonyms and antonyms, from the Free Dictionary API (Wiktionary).

name: translate_text
label: Translating
description: Translates text (up to 500 characters with MyMemory; longer when the user set up LibreTranslate) into a language, detecting the source. For a Telegram message use translate_message instead.

name: wikipedia_search
label: Searching Wikipedia
description: Searches Wikipedia articles, with a short description, the first sentences and a picture for each.

name: wikipedia_summary
label: Reading Wikipedia
description: The summary of one Wikipedia article (the closest match when the title isn't exact), with its picture and link.

name: wikipedia_on_this_day
label: Checking on this day
description: What happened on a date in history from Wikipedia: selected events, or all events, births, deaths and holidays.

name: sports_scores
label: Checking scores
description: Live scores, results and fixtures for a league on a day (default today) from ESPN: soccer (Premier League, LaLiga, Serie A, Bundesliga, Ligue 1, Champions League and more), NBA, WNBA, NFL, MLB, NHL and college leagues. Each game has its status, score, scorers or top performers, venue and TV. The user sees a scoreboard and can tap a game for the full match; use sports_match for one game.

name: sports_match
label: Opening a match
description: One game in full: score, status, goals, cards and substitutions with minutes, team stats side by side (possession, shots…), lineups with formations, or top performers for other sports, venue and attendance. Needs the event id from sports_scores or sports_team.

name: sports_standings
label: Checking the table
description: A league table or conference standings: position, played, won, drawn, lost, goal difference and points (soccer), or win %, games behind, streak and last ten (US sports), with qualification and relegation zones.

name: sports_team
label: Looking up a team
description: A team: position and record, form (last five), recent results and next games, with its crest and colours.

name: sports_player
label: Looking up a player
description: A player or athlete in any sport from TheSportsDB: photo, team and national team, position, number, nationality, age and birthplace, height and weight, and a biography.

name: sports_news
label: Reading sports news
description: The latest ESPN headlines for a league, with pictures and links.

name: sports_top_scorers
label: Checking top scorers
description: The goal scorers table of a football competition with goals, assists, penalties and games, from football-data.org. Needs the free football-data.org key the user adds in Settings.

name: formula1
label: Checking Formula 1
description: Formula 1 from Jolpica (Ergast): next (the next Grand Prix with every session time and the championship leader), standings (drivers), constructors, last_race (full classification) or calendar (the season).

name: system_check
label: Running a system check
description: Checks everything the app depends on and reports what works, what is broken and what could be better, with a health score out of 100: AI keys and models, Telegram accounts (TDLib, two-step verification, unknown sessions), decisions, MCP servers, skills, connected apps, the phone and its connection (storage, memory, battery saver, network, DNS), watches and the check-in, routines (failed or stalled runs), privacy (app lock, approvals, what Block & mute hides), home-screen widgets, voice, tools and usage, money and call data, and upkeep (memories, briefs, backups, storage). It only reads. Use it when something isn't working, or the user asks how the app or phone is doing. The user sees a card with the score and a sheet with every finding, so answer with what matters most and how to fix it, not the whole list. A full check can take half a minute; give areas to check only some.

name: list_hidden
label: Checking Block & mute
description: What Block & mute hides: the channels and groups blocked on this phone, the muted words, how many accounts are blocked on Telegram (list_blocked lists them), whether hidden messages leave a "tap to view" notice or disappear, and whether archived chats are filtered too.

name: block_chat
label: Blocking a channel or group
description: Blocks a channel or group on this phone (Telegram itself can't block a chat you're in): the user stays in it and can still open it, but posts forwarded from it into other chats, and what it posts in comments and groups, are hidden. For people and bots use block_user. Undo with unblock_chat.

name: unblock_chat
label: Unblocking a channel or group
description: Unblocks a channel or group blocked with block_chat, so its posts show again. list_hidden lists them.

name: mute_words
label: Muting words
description: Mutes words or phrases: messages and posts containing one are hidden in chats, groups, channels and comments (the user's own messages never are). Matching ignores case and is whole-word, so "cat" doesn't hide "education". Undo with unmute_words.

name: unmute_words
label: Unmuting words
description: Unmutes words muted with mute_words, or every muted word with all: true. list_hidden lists them.

name: block_mute_settings
label: Changing Block & mute
description: How Block & mute hides things: for each of blocked accounts, blocked chats and muted words, whether a hidden message leaves a "tap to view" notice (true) or disappears without a trace (false); and whether archived chats are filtered too. Leave out what shouldn't change.

name: screen_status
label: Checking screen control
description: Whether screen control is on (Triangle under Android Settings → Accessibility), and which app is on the screen now. If it is off, tell the user how to turn it on: Settings → Screen control in Triangle.

name: screen_read
label: Reading the screen
description: What is on the phone's screen now, in any app: the app, and its elements (id, role like button/field/text/switch/list, text, label, hint, whether it is clickable, editable, scrollable, checked, focused, disabled, and bounds in pixels). Use the ids with screen_tap, screen_type and screen_scroll. Read again after anything changes the screen: ids only last until the next read. Passwords are never shown. Give query to list only elements whose text, label or hint contains it. To use an app: open_app, screen_read, then act, reading again to check each step worked. Triangle's own screens, Android's permission screens and the apps the user put off limits can't be read.

name: screen_screenshot
label: Taking a screenshot
description: Takes a screenshot of the phone's screen (Android 11 or newer) and saves it on the phone. To look at it, call view_image with the returned image_path. Prefer screen_read, which is exact and cheaper; use this for pictures, maps, games or apps whose elements read as empty. Some apps (banking, private tabs) block it.

name: screen_wait
label: Waiting for the screen
description: Waits until text appears on the screen, or (without text) until the screen changes: after opening an app, sending something or loading a page. Then read the screen.

name: screen_tap
label: Tapping on the screen
description: Taps an element in the app on screen: by id from screen_read (best), by its visible text, or at a point (x, y as fractions of the screen) when nothing else works. long_press for a long press. Returns which app is on screen after and whether it changed; read the screen again to see the result.

name: screen_type
label: Typing on the screen
description: Types text into a text field of the app on screen: the field's id from screen_read, or the field that has focus. Replaces what is there unless append is true. submit presses the keyboard's action key (search, send, go) after, on Android 11 or newer. Never for passwords: those fields refuse, and the user types them.

name: screen_scroll
label: Scrolling the screen
description: Scrolls a list or page in the app on screen: down shows what is below, up what is above, left and right for carousels and tabs. Scrolls the given element, or the largest scrollable area. Read the screen after.

name: screen_swipe
label: Swiping on the screen
description: Swipes from one point to another (fractions of the screen): to dismiss, reveal swipe actions, move a slider or turn pages when screen_scroll doesn't. Swipes can delete or archive in some apps, so say what it does in why.

name: screen_press
label: Pressing a phone button
description: Presses a system button: back, home, recents (the app switcher), notifications (pulls down the shade), quick_settings, or lock (locks the screen).

name: jev_decide
label: Deciding with Jev
description: Asks TypeSafe Jev several typed questions about one piece of content at once: yes/no (noul), one of named options (choice), a rubric score (score). Returns calibrated probabilities, not prose. Use it to classify, route, triage, moderate or grade consistently, and keep to the thresholds in the answer (yes, uncertain).

name: jev_batch
label: Deciding a batch with Jev
description: Asks Jev the same questions about many items in ONE call (up to 100): the sentiment of the last messages in a chat, the topic of each email, a score per review. Returns a short answer per item plus totals (counts per choice, yes/no counts, mean score). Always use this for two or more items instead of one Jev call per item; pass each item id (e.g. the message id) to match the answers back.

name: jev_noul
label: Jev yes/no
description: One yes/no question to Jev about one item: the probability it is true, and yes at your threshold. For two or more items use jev_batch.

name: jev_choice
label: Jev choice
description: Jev picks one of several named options for one item, with each option's probability and its confidence. For two or more items use jev_batch.

name: jev_score
label: Jev score
description: Jev rates one item on a rubric: the probability-weighted level, each level's probability, and confidence. For two or more items use jev_batch.

name: jev_box
label: Jev box
description: Jev finds something in a picture and returns its box: top, bottom, left and right as fractions of the picture from its top-left. Give the picture in images.

name: jev_models
label: Listing Jev models
description: The Jev model ids your TypeSafe key can use (aliases like jev-latest and pinned versions).

name: mcp_search
label: Searching MCP servers
description: Searches the official MCP Registry for servers that add tools (GitHub, Linear, docs, databases…). Returns each server's registry name, what it does, how it connects, and the values it needs (inputs).

name: mcp_list_servers
label: Listing MCP servers
description: The MCP servers installed in the app: id, transport and address. Doesn't connect to them.

name: mcp_is_installed
label: Checking an MCP server
description: Whether an MCP server id is installed. Doesn't connect.

name: mcp_install_catalog
label: Installing an MCP server
description: Installs a server from the MCP Registry by its full name (from mcp_search). Give the values its inputs ask for (API keys) in headers, by header or variable name. Servers that run as a local command can only be added by the person in Settings. Asks first.

name: mcp_install
label: Adding an MCP server
description: Saves an MCP server by address: a Streamable HTTP (or legacy SSE) endpoint and optional headers. Plain http only for localhost or the local network. Doesn't connect yet. Asks first.

name: mcp_uninstall
label: Removing an MCP server
description: Removes an installed MCP server and its saved headers, and closes its connection.

name: mcp_list_tools
label: Opening an MCP server
description: Connects to an installed MCP server and lists its tools with their input schemas, for mcp_call_tool.

name: mcp_call_tool
label: Using an MCP tool
description: Runs one tool on an installed MCP server, with arguments matching its input schema from mcp_list_tools. Works right after installing. It can do anything the server allows, so it asks first.

name: mcp_list_resources
label: Listing MCP resources
description: Connects to an installed MCP server and lists the resources (files, records, pages) it offers.

name: mcp_read_resource
label: Reading an MCP resource
description: Reads one resource from an installed MCP server.

name: mcp_list_prompts
label: Listing MCP prompts
description: Connects to an installed MCP server and lists its prompt templates and their arguments.

name: mcp_get_prompt
label: Loading an MCP prompt
description: Loads a prompt template from an installed MCP server, filled with its arguments.

name: search_skills
label: Searching skills
description: Searches public skill catalogs (Skyll and skills.sh) for Agent Skills: step-by-step instructions for a kind of task. Returns what each does, its source, installs, and the install string for install_skill.

name: list_skills
label: Listing skills
description: Installed skills: name, what each is for, where it came from and its bundled files.

name: is_skill_installed
label: Checking a skill
description: Whether a skill is installed.

name: preview_skill
label: Previewing a skill
description: Reads a skill from GitHub or a SKILL.md link without installing it: its instructions and bundled files.

name: load_skill
label: Using a skill
description: Loads an installed skill's full instructions. Call it before doing a task a skill covers, then follow them.

name: read_skill_file
label: Reading a skill file
description: Reads a reference file or script bundled with an installed skill.

name: install_skill
label: Installing a skill
description: Installs a skill from GitHub (owner/repo or owner/repo@skill-name) or an https link to a SKILL.md, so its instructions are available in every chat. Asks first.

name: uninstall_skill
label: Removing a skill
description: Removes an installed skill and its bundled files from the app.
